text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The closing of telecoms group Ericsson's printed board production in Norrkoping, Sweden is only the first step in the company's plans to outsource operations. Some 8,000 more jobs are in danger. Unions say the motivation behind moving the printed board operations to Scotland is low wages and miserable working conditions. U.S. high-tech companies are also outsourcing component production and setting the industry trend.

- Denmark should join the European economic and monetary union (EMU) because membership will mean more freedom and influence for the country than staying outside the group, leader of Danish metal workers' union Max Baehring says in an interview. Higher interest rates, decreased foreign investments and fewer new jobs will result from Denmark's, like Sweden's, choice to stay outside EMU from its planned 1999 start.
- Published only on Fridays during the summer.
